channel.title: The Cartographer blog
channel.description: Short, cited articles from Team Cartographer on working with coding agents, with sources.

item.title: Your agent's session history expires: what to keep, and when
item.description: Claude Code deletes old session transcripts after 30 days by default. Here's what that means for the record of your build, and a simple way to keep it.

item.title: Ironies of automation: staying sharp when an agent writes the code
item.description: Bainbridge warned in 1983 that automation can erode the skills needed to supervise it. A 2026 trial of AI-assisted coding suggests a similar worry.

item.title: Feeling fast versus being fast: timing your agent-assisted work
item.description: Developers in one trial felt faster with AI and measured slower. What that and the planning fallacy suggest about timing your own agent sessions.

item.title: Writing a spec before the prompt: what the research says
item.description: Vague requirements are an old problem, and agents don't remove it. What a requirements survey and Anthropic's docs say about writing the spec first.

item.title: When to start a fresh session: long chats with a coding agent
item.description: Long agent sessions get heavy. What Anthropic's own docs say about context, /clear, /compact and rewind, and a plain rule for when to start over.

item.title: Write down the why: decision records for agent-built code
item.description: Code shows what you chose, not why. What Nygard and Microsoft's guidance say about decision records, and a ten second habit for agent sessions.

item.title: Praise is not evidence: appraising an agent's work honestly
item.description: A confident all-done feels like proof, but it isn't. What research and vendor docs say about checking an agent's work against evidence, not tone.

item.title: Reading your own dead ends: what abandoned work can teach
item.description: Abandoned branches and rewound sessions are the part of a build nobody keeps. Here's why they're worth reading, and what the docs say about keeping them.

item.title: Declaring done before you start: goals as a yardstick
item.description: Decide what finished looks like before your first prompt. What Scrum and vendor docs say about done, and how to write a yardstick an agent can check.

item.title: Why a correction is the most informative prompt in a session
item.description: A correction tells you what you meant, what the agent assumed, and where they split. Here's what research and vendor docs say, and how to read yours.

item.title: What the research says about reviewing code you didn't write
item.description: Two studies of code review put understanding the change first. Here's what they found, and what it means when you didn't write the code.
